api_key.description: User API key. Could use `CTFD_API_KEY` environment variable instead. Despite being the most convenient way to authenticate yourself, we do not recommend it as you will probably generate a long-live token without any rotation policy.

password.description: The administrator or service account password to login with. Could use `CTFD_ADMIN_PASSWORD` environment variable instead.

url.description: CTFd base URL (e.g. `https://my-ctf.lan`). Could use `CTFD_URL` environment variable instead.

username.description: The administrator or service account username to login with. Could use `CTFD_ADMIN_USERNAME` environment variable instead.

block.description:
Use the Terraform Provider to interact with a [CTFd](https://github.com/ctfd/ctfd).

## Why creating this ?

Terraform is used to manage resources that have lifecycles, configurations, to sum it up.

That is the case of CTFd: it handles challenges that could be created, modified and deleted.
With some work to leverage the unsteady CTFd's API, Terraform is now able to manage them as cloud resources bringing you to opportunity of CTF as Code.

With a paradigm-shifting vision of setting up CTFs, the Terraform Provider for CTFd avoid shitty scripts, `ctfcli` and other tools that does not solve the problem of reproductibility, ease of deployment and resiliency.

## Authentication

You must configure the provider with the proper credentials before you can use it.

If you are using the username/password configuration, remember that CTFd comes with a
ratelimiter on rare methods and endpoints, but `POST /login` is one of them.
This could lead to unexpected failures under intensive work.

!> **Warning:** Hard-coded credentials are not recommended in any Terraform
configuration and risks secret leakage should this file ever be committed to a
public version control system.

minimum.description: The minimum points for a dynamic-score challenge to reach with the decay function. Once there, no solve could have more value.

position.description: The challenge position as displayed to players.

value.description: The value (points) of the challenge once solved. It is mapped to `initial` under the hood, but displayed as `value` for consistency with the standard challenge.

CTFd is built around the Challenge resource, which contains all the attributes to define a part of the Capture The Flag event.

This implementation has support of a more dynamic behavior for its scoring through time/solves thus is different from a standard challenge.

CTFd is built around the Challenge resource, which contains all the attributes to define a part of the Capture The Flag event.

It is the first historic implementation of its kind, with basic functionalities.

contentb64.description: Base 64 content of the file, perfectly fit the use-cases of complex binaries. You could provide it from the file-system using `filebase64("${path.module}/...")`.

id.description: Identifier of the file, used internally to handle the CTFd corresponding object. WARNING: updating this file does not work, requires full replacement.

location.description: Location where the file is stored on the CTFd instance, for download purposes.

name.description: Name of the file as displayed to end-users.

sha1sum.description: The sha1 sum of the file.

block.description: A CTFd file for a challenge.

content.description: The actual flag to match. Consider using the convention `MYCTF{value}` with `MYCTF` being the shortcode of your event's name and `value` depending on each challenge.

data.description: The flag sensitivity information, either case_sensitive or case_insensitive

id.description: Identifier of the flag, used internally to handle the CTFd corresponding object.

type.description: The type of the flag, could be either static or regex

block.description: A flag to solve the challenge.

content.description: Content of the hint as displayed to the end-user.

cost.description: Cost of the hint, and if any specified, the end-user will consume its own (or team) points to get it.

id.description: Identifier of the hint, used internally to handle the CTFd corresponding object.

requirements.description: List of the other hints it depends on.

title.description: Title of the hint, displayed to end users before unlocking.

block.description: A hint for a challenge to help players solve it.

content.description: The solution to the challenge, in markdown.

id.description: Identifier of the solution, used internally to handle the CTFd corresponding object.

state.description: State of the solution, either hidden or visible.

affiliation.description: Affiliation to a company or agency.

banned.description: Is true if the team is banned from the CTF.

bracket_id.description: The bracket id the user plays in.

captain.description: Member who is captain of the team. Must be part of the members too. Note it could cause a fatal error in case of resource import with an inconsistent CTFd configuration i.e. if a team has no captain yet (should not be possible).

country.description: Country the team represent or is hail from.

hidden.description: Is true if the team is hidden to the participants.

members.description: List of members (User), defined by their IDs.

password.description: Password of the team. Notice that during a CTF you may not want to update those to avoid defaulting team accesses.

website.description: Website, blog, or anything similar (displayed to other participants).

block.description: CTFd defines a Team as a group of Users who will attend the Capture The Flag event.

banned.description: Is true if the user is banned from the CTF.

country.description: Country the user represent or is native from.

email.description: Email of the user, may be used to verify the account.

hidden.description: Is true if the user is hidden to the participants.

language.description: Language the user is fluent in.

name.description: Name or pseudo of the user.

verified.description: Is true if the user has verified its account by email, or if set by an admin.

website.description: Website, blog, or anything similar (displayed to other participants).
